svg.title: Shrinkwrap: pull points onto another object's surface
svg.desc: In edit mode, Shrinkwrap pushes the selected points out from the middle of a chosen target object until each meets its surface. Both meshes are brought into the target's space, the mesh's middle is moved onto the target's middle, a spatial grid finds where each ray from the middle hits the target's triangles (closest spot if it misses), and the result goes back as one undo step that changes only the positions.
svg.text: Shrinkwrap (retopology, second step)
Lay a rough, clean mesh over a dense one: every point is pushed out from the middle until it meets the target.
1. Pick a target
In edit mode, choose an object in
Wrap onto (any shape, mesh or
imported model, as it is shown now:
modifiers, position, turn and size
are included).
2. Same space
Selected points (all if none) go from
the edited mesh's space to world, then
into the target's own space (inverse
of its matrix), so both meshes can
be compared whatever their transforms.
3. Ray from the middle hits the surface
A uniform grid holds the target's
triangles; each point searches its cell,
then ring by ring, until nothing closer
can exist. Exact (tested against brute
force); fast for 100 000 triangles.
4. Back and store
The snapped points go back to the edited
mesh's space. Only positions change:
triangles, seams, creases and the UV map
stay. One undo step (stored as a patch
when the mesh is big).
Not built yet
An offset above the surface and
a keep-distance mode.
Snapping while you move points
(a live Retopo mode) and the strip tool.
Wrapping onto a model with many parts.
